title: Unnithan's attack on Shafi, invocation of Chandy mask new KC-VD power struggle in Congress
content: Kasaragod: Amal Unnithan, Kasaragod's outspoken MP Rajmohan Unnithan's son, put out a baffling Facebook post on Tuesday, in which he accused Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala of having a hand in the raging factional feud in Keralam Congress. The junior Unnithan said that after orchestrating the feud, Chennithala was now keeping away from the ensuing controversy. He was responding to the relentless online attack on his father. Yet, Amal going after Chennithala left Congress watchers puzzled. But Rajmohan Unnithan, who spent Tuesday taking on fellow MP Shafi Parambil and threatening to embarrass him with damning revelations, cleared the air over his son's post later that evening. He said his son had not understood the shifting loyalties within the party and did not realise that some of those he believed were aligned with Chennithala and attacking him had already moved to another camp. The explanation offered a telling glimpse into the fluid realignments within the Keralam Congress, where old factional labels have lost their meaning and leaders are repositioning themselves around two new centres of influence- AICC general secretary K C Venugopal in the party organisation and Chief Minister V D Satheesan in the government. The invocation of late Oommen Chandy and his erstwhile A group in the slugfest serves as a smokescreen for a wider struggle for influence over appointments and a say in who occupies key positions in the party, including the KPCC president's post. Unnithan, who was earlier perceived to be close to Venugopal, is moving towards Satheesan, according to Congress insiders. His growing proximity to the Chief Minister has coincided with a bitter confrontation with Shafi Parambil, a working president of the KPCC, and a sustained counterattack on him by sections of the Youth Congress and the Kasaragod District Congress Committee (DCC). Unnithal decided to blunt the cyber attack on him by accusing Parambil and those claiming to be from the 'school of Oommen Chandy politics' of having abandoned him during the solar-case controversy. A shift in allegiance A Congress insider and confidant of Unnithan says the MP's growing proximity to Satheesan has two explanations. Unnithan had hoped to become KPCC president but did not receive the backing he expected from Venugopal. He also believes that DCC president P K Faisal is being protected by Venugopal through Revenue Minister A P Anilkumar, who, according to the insider, is Venugopal's point person in the state. The same source claims that Venugopal's camp grew wary after realising that Unnithan was moving closer to Satheesan. He alleges that Faisal was encouraged to take on the MP aggressively, and that the Youth Congress attacks were part of a wider effort to contain him. The dispute also reflects a parallel power struggle over who gets to influence appointments in Kasaragod. Faisal has complained that the Chief Minister disregards the DCC's recommendations and listens only to the MP. Recently, the government snubbed the DCC's recommendations and appointed three additional government pleaders, all picked by the MP. Unnithan, meanwhile, has been seeking Faisal's removal as DCC president, an attempt that has met resistance from the Venugopal camp. Unnithan's shift also reflects a larger calculation. A political observer who follows the Congress closely says the old A-group structure has fragmented, with individual leaders now gravitating towards whichever power centre they believe can protect their interests. The observer identifies Venugopal and Satheesan as the two principal centres of influence, with the party organisation and the government increasingly operating through separate channels. '2020 and flat in Kochi' Unnithan tried to discredit Shafi Parambi by alleging that he did not belong to the A group, founded by the late Oommen Chandy. He said only K C Joseph and Benny Behanan were staunch A-group leaders...
